focus.jbig: Micron beat lifts tech, 10Y at ~5.29%, jobs report tomorrow · one thin Type A boarded
focus.jtag: Micron's blowout AMC print lifts AI/semis, but 5.29% yields and Friday's jobs report keep the tape selective — scanner boarded only MKC
focus.jnote: The tape is split in two this morning. On the micro side, Micron reported a blowout fiscal Q4 after the bell — EPS of $33.42 vs ~$31.8 expected, revenue of $54.23B, and a Q1 guide (~$61.5B revenue, ~$38.15 EPS) well above Street — reigniting the AI-memory trade and lifting Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom; Nasdaq-100 futures are up ~0.6–1.0%. On the macro side, the 10-year yield sits near ~5.29% (30Y above 5.6%), a multi-decade high, which keeps pressure on rate-sensitive groups. Oil eased toward WTI ~$89–90 on recovering Gulf exports and US–Iran talks, and gold firmed toward ~$4,200. The dominant forward catalyst is Friday's long-delayed September jobs report (8:30 ET). This is a headline-and-data tape, not one a Sniper sells premium into.
focus.notdown: AI / semis (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MU) are the clear bid after Micron's beat-and-raise — the memory shortage and AI-capex story is durable. But chasing a one-day earnings pop with a bull put into a 5.29%-yield tape and a jobs report tomorrow is not a clean Sniper: a hot payrolls print or a yield spike gaps growth down fast. Watch-only, not a table-pounder.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near multi-decade highs. But selling bear calls into Friday's jobs report carries violent squeeze risk on any soft-labor headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~61 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 38% is above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. Decisively, the September jobs report inside the next 24h is a market-moving release that cannot be GREEN under the rules, stacked on a bond market at ~5.29% multi-decade-high yields. The scanner boarded a single Type A (MKC) — but on just 0.06× relative volume, far below the 1.3× confirmation bar. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the jobs window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: McCormick reported Q3 pre-market and the system boarded it bullish on the confirmed price reaction. The print itself was a beat — adjusted EPS ~$0.86 vs ~$0.76 est and revenue ~$2.02B vs ~$1.98B, helped by the Mexico acquisition — and the gap is holding (~+3.8% to ~$48.18 vs $46.40 prior close). But be honest about the flags: relative volume is only ~0.06×, far below the 1.3× confirmation bar, and the pending Unilever foods-business deal is under UK antitrust review, an unresolved overhead. The options-implied move was ~6.3% vs a realised ~3.8% gap. Four S/R layers sit within 7% below price (swing $47.30, gap floor $46.40, swings $45.74 and $44.82).
setups.check_note: On a RED day don’t force it. If taken, confirm at 9:35 that price holds > open AND > $46.40 prior close with price in the upper third of range — the 0.06× volume is a real concern, so half size at most.

risks: September jobs report · Fri 10/2, 8:30 ET — the long-delayed payrolls print (originally scheduled Oct 3) lands tomorrow into a rate-pressured tape. Both a hot and a too-soft number carry gap risk into the weekend. This is the number-one thing to watch.

Bond yields — 10Y near ~5.29%, 30Y above 5.6%, both multi-decade highs — driven by inflation expectations, hawkish Fed repricing and deficit worries. A further spike hits rate-sensitive growth, REITs, utilities and small caps hardest.

Micron read-through — the AI-memory beat-and-raise lifts the whole semis complex (NVDA, AMD, AVGO), but the muted stock reaction shows how much optimism is already priced; a semis reversal would drag the tape.

MKC single-name gap risk — the just-boarded McCormick reaction is on only ~0.06× volume and the pending Unilever foods deal is under UK antitrust review; thin confirmation plus merger overhang means the gap can unwind.
US–Iran & the Strait of Hormuz — oil eased on recovering Gulf exports and ongoing talks, but the standoff is unresolved; any breakdown sends crude (and inflation fear) vertical.
